name: CEGO
description: Cego: German Tarock from Baden; 3–4p, 54-card Cego deck (22 trumps + 32 in 4 suits). Central hand (Legage/Cego); many contracts use Legage. Developed from Ombre and Dreierles. Two-phase bidding; declarer may play from Cego (central hand); follow suit, must trump if unable to follow; 70 card points total, bidder needs 36+ to win normal contracts.

content.text: Cego: German Tarock from Baden; 3–4p, 54-card Cego deck (22 trumps + 32 in 4 suits). Central hand (Legage/Cego); many contracts use Legage. Developed from Ombre and Dreierles. Two-phase bidding; declarer may play from Cego (central hand); follow suit, must trump if unable to follow; 70 card points total, bidder needs 36+ to win normal contracts.

Germany (Baden, Hohenzollern). Cego developed early 19th c. from Dreierles and Ombre (Napoleonic Wars). 54-card Cego deck; central hand (Legage). National game of Baden; only German region where genuine Tarok cards remain in general use.
54-card Cego deck (22 trumps Trocke + 8 per suit).
Varies by contract; central hand (Legage) dealt; many contracts use Legage. Anticlockwise.

items.text: Pflicht-Räuber: Compulsory round of Räuber at fixed time (e.g. 23:00); one deal per player, no other bidding. Loser pays; if one player takes no tricks loser pays 60; stakes multiply after the round.

Ministranten Version: Bräunlingen variant: Vorhand can choose Cego, Piccolo, Bettel, Geregelter Räuber, Wilder Räuber or Dresch when all pass. Stricter rules for Eine Leere / Zwei Leere (must lead exposed cards; bidder leads after first trick(s)).
